theme: 3 terms for styling text in SwiftUI: how many lines, which color and a string with styles inside

terms.definition: A modifier that sets the maximum number of lines a text can use.
terms.example: Set a Line Limit of two, so the title never gets too tall.
terms.code:
Text("A very long title for the card")
    .lineLimit(2)

terms.definition: A modifier that sets the color or gradient used to draw text and shapes.
terms.example: Use Foreground Style to make the price red.

terms.definition: A string that stores styles, such as colors and links, for parts of the text.
terms.example: Use an AttributedString for the link inside the sentence.

Today's terms

landscape.hook: Can you explain Line Limit, Foreground Style and AttributedString in English?

dialogue.title: The long product title

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my product title is too long and pushes the price down.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Set a Line Limit. It is the maximum number of lines a text can use.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I wrote `.lineLimit(1)`, and now the title ends with three dots.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. The Line Limit cuts the text, so show the full name on the detail screen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now I want colored text, and later a link inside the same text.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use an AttributedString. It stores styles for parts of the text.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Then you show it with `Text(s)`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is Foreground Style. It sets the color for the whole view.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So which one wins, the AttributedString or the Foreground Style?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The style inside the AttributedString wins for that part of the text.

dialogue.code:
var s = AttributedString("Sale today")
s.foregroundColor = .red
Text(s)
    .foregroundStyle(.blue)
    .lineLimit(1)
